sections.overview: This purple sea urchin is a common echinoderm of the northeast Pacific rocky shore.
sections.identification: Its round test bears movable purple spines, tube feet and tiny pincers called pedicellariae.
sections.habitat: It ranges from Vancouver Island to Isla Cedros, Baja California, on rocky shores.
sections.diet: It grazes red, brown and green algae, including kelp where available.
sections.behavior: Its spines and tube feet help it move, hold on and handle food.
sections.reproduction: Adults release eggs and sperm into the water for external fertilization; planktonic larvae later settle.
sections.ecology: When populations become unusually dense, grazing can reduce kelp forests and create urchin barrens.
sections.conservation: These local overabundance events are an ecosystem-management issue, not evidence of a global decline of the species.
